title: Energy levels of an electron in a 1 nm infinite well
caption: E_n = n²h²/8mL² = n² × 0.38 eV. The levels are not evenly spaced (E₂ = 4E₁, E₃ = 9E₁), the lowest is above zero, and jumps between them give photons: 2 → 1 is 1.13 eV (1099 nm, infrared), 3 → 2 is 1.88 eV (659 nm, red) and 4 → 3 is 2.63 eV (471 nm, blue).
alt: Energy-level diagram for an electron in a 1 nm well: levels at 0.38, 1.50, 3.38 and 6.02 electronvolts with downward arrows for the transitions 2 to 1, 3 to 2 and 4 to 3.
description: Horizontal levels for n = 1 to 4 at heights E_n = n² × h²/8mL² with L = 1 nm: 0.38 eV, 1.50 eV, 3.38 eV, 6.02 eV.
The spacings grow with n (1 : 3 : 5 : 7 in units of E₁) and the lowest level is above zero: the zero-point energy.
Arrows show photon emission: 2 → 1 gives 1.13 eV, 1099 nm in the infrared; 3 → 2 gives 659 nm, red; 4 → 3 gives 471 nm, blue.
